title: Bucić–Sudakov–Tran Conjecture (multidimensional Erdős–Szekeres)
statement_text: A doubly exponential upper bound holds for the multidimensional Erdős–Szekeres numbers $M_d(n)$ in every dimension $d$.
context_text: Fishburn and Graham proved a multidimensional Erdős–Szekeres theorem in 1993, and Bucić, Sudakov, and Tran later established doubly exponential upper bounds for $d=2,3$ while conjecturing such bounds extend to all dimensions. The present paper's Theorem 1.4 provides a doubly exponential upper bound for $d\geq 4$, improving on the previous triply exponential upper bound of Bucić–Sudakov–Tran.
paper_contribution: Confirms the conjecture by proving a doubly exponential upper bound on $M_d(n)$ for all $d\geq 4$, improving the previously known triply exponential upper bound.

title: Problem 4.1
context_text: The Cartesian product $G\square H$ has vertex set $V(G)\times V(H)$, with $(x,y)$ adjacent to $(x',y')$ iff $x=x'$ and $yy'\in E(H)$, or $xx'\in E(G)$ and $y=y'$; in the $d$-fold product $\square^dK_N$ of copies of $K_N$, an edge joining two vertices that differ only in coordinate $i$ is in direction $i$. A colouring of the edges of $\square^dK_n$ is monochromatic in every direction if, for each $i$, all edges in direction $i$ have the same colour (colours may differ between directions). $R_r(d,n)$ is the least $N$ such that every $r$-colouring of the edges of $\square^dK_N$ contains a copy of $\square^dK_n$ that is monochromatic in every direction. Iterating Ramsey's theorem gives a tower-type bound; the authors prove the doubly exponential bound $R_r(d,n)\le r^{r^{C_drn^d}}$, whereas random colourings only give a singly exponential lower bound. They ask whether there is a simple exponential upper bound or the numbers grow faster. The problem is stated in the paper as 'Fix $r,d\ge2$. Is $R_2(2,n)$ superexponential in $n$?'; the quantifier over $r,d$ suggests that $R_r(d,n)$ in general is meant, with $R_2(2,n)$ (two colours, two dimensions) as the first case.

title: Problem 4.2
statement_text: Does there exist $C>0$ such that $\log R_{2}(2,n)\leq(\log M_{2}(n))^{C}$?
context_text: The Cartesian product $G\square H$ has vertex set $V(G)\times V(H)$, with $(x,y)$ adjacent to $(x',y')$ iff $x=x'$ and $yy'\in E(H)$, or $xx'\in E(G)$ and $y=y'$; in the $d$-fold product $\square^dK_N$ of copies of $K_N$, an edge joining two vertices that differ only in coordinate $i$ is in direction $i$. A colouring of the edges of $\square^dK_n$ is monochromatic in every direction if, for each $i$, all edges in direction $i$ have the same colour (colours may differ between directions). $R_r(d,n)$ is the least $N$ such that every $r$-colouring of the edges of $\square^dK_N$ contains a copy of $\square^dK_n$ that is monochromatic in every direction. A $d$-dimensional array is an injective function $f:A_1\times\dots\times A_d\to\mathbb{R}$ with $A_i\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$; it is monotone if, for each direction $i$, all its $1$-dimensional subarrays in direction $i$ are increasing, or all are decreasing. $M_d(n)$, the multidimensional Erdős–Szekeres number of Fishburn and Graham, is the least $N$ such that every $d$-dimensional array on $[N]^d$ contains a monotone subarray of size $[n]^d$. Colouring an edge $xy$ according to whether $f(x)<f(y)$ shows $M_2(n)\le R_2(2,n)$. Bucić, Sudakov and Tran proved $M_2(n)\le2^{2^{(2+o(1))n}}$ and doubly exponential bounds for $d=3$; the authors prove $R_r(d,n)\le r^{r^{C_drn^d}}$ and $M_d(n)\le2^{n^{C_dn^{d-1}}}$ for all $d$, but for both quantities a gap between singly and doubly exponential bounds remains. The authors ask whether $R_2(2,n)$ can be bounded above by a function of $M_2(n)$, for example by this polynomial relation between the logarithms.
